ai.summary: AMD reported a $1.07 billion non-cash charge tied to warrants granted under chip-supply agreements with OpenAI and Meta. The deals illustrate how AI companies and chipmakers are increasingly using equity incentives to secure large, long-term purchases.
ai.title: AMD's OpenAI, Meta chip deals trigger $1 billion quarterly charge

ai.summary: AMD reported record third-quarter revenue of $13.4 billion, with data-center sales reaching $8.5 billion. The company forecast about $17 billion in fourth-quarter revenue and said it expects revenue growth above 80% in 2027, driven chiefly by data centers.
ai.title: AMD rides data center riches to ‘largest and most profitable’ quarter in history

ai.summary: The New York Times and, in a separate lawsuit, the New York Daily News, Chicago Tribune and Orlando Sentinel sued Brave on November 2. The complaints allege unauthorized use of journalism and sales of content to AI companies; these are allegations, not court findings.
ai.title: New York Times and three newspapers sue Brave over alleged AI content scraping

ai.summary: MeitY released EKA-1 and Dhīr 2B and 5B on November 3 under the IndiaAI Mission. The government describes EKA-1 as a multilingual model for math, code and reasoning, and the smaller Dhīr models as offline-capable assistants, including on-device mobile use. These are launch claims, not independently verified performance results.
ai.title: IndiaAI Mission's three indigenous AI models target offline mobile access, secure use in critical sectors

ai.summary: Anthropic's November 2 research release describes FlashProve, a prototype for cryptographically checking that committed model weights produced an output. Its demonstrated mixture-of-experts configuration carries substantial proving overhead; this is intermediate research, not a general-purpose production verification service.
ai.title: Anthropic releases FlashProve inference-verification prototype

quantum.summary: IBM’s Quantum Nighthawk processor has been installed at Yonsei University, its first deployment at a customer institution’s own facility. IBM reports 120 programmable qubits and more than 100,000 circuits per second, with 25 times the circuit throughput of Eagle. This is a vendor-reported hardware capability, not demonstrated commercial advantage.
quantum.title: IBM installs latest quantum processor at Yonsei University, enabling 100,000 circuits per second

quantum.summary: In a preprint submitted November 2, NVIDIA researchers describe an AI-assisted, Lean-verified workflow linking error-correction code spaces to a superconducting device model. The eight-qubit demonstration is a modeled hardware-engineering result, not an experimental QPU performance or commercial-advantage claim.
quantum.title: Agentic Pipelines for Mapping Topological Codes to Quantum Hardware

quantum.summary: Coverage of a November 2 preprint describes MBUndo, a compiler pass that converts circuits to measurement-based uncomputation. On 22 benchmarks, the authors report T-gate-count reductions above 36.5% compared with existing uncomputation synthesizers. This is a compiler benchmark, not a measured production speedup.
quantum.title: Researchers Show How To Automatically Uncompute Ancilla Qubits With Measurements

quantum.summary: A preprint first submitted November 2 and revised November 3 estimates that advantage for the examined spin SYK-dot-chain ground-state simulations could require dots of roughly 15–21 or more qubits and two-qubit gate errors around 10⁻⁶. This is a workload-specific resource estimate, not a universal threshold for quantum advantage.
quantum.title: A Quantum Advantage May Need Two-qubit Gates With 10⁻⁶ Error Rates

quantum.summary: Quint Computing's €9.1 million initial financing was announced November 3 to support development of superconducting quantum processors. Investor Quantonation separately reports a €2.2 million EIC grant. The proposed reduction in error-correction overhead is a development goal, not a demonstrated commercial result.
quantum.title: VC funding deals: Syncere, Quint Computing, Tumbleweed

quantum.summary: Coverage of a November 2 preprint introduces eigenkit, a common interface across 12 simulator and hardware execution providers. The authors report experiments on IBM Heron and IQM Emerald showing that processor suitability depends on the algorithm and its match to hardware connectivity. This supports portability, not general quantum advantage.
quantum.title: A Single Library Now Links Quantum Algorithms To IBM And IQM Hardware
